q: 1. The length of pre-cast concrete piles varies from
explain: Modern pre-casting and transport capabilities allow for pile lengths up to 30 meters. Lengths beyond this typically require specialized mechanical joints or cast-in-situ methods.

q: 2. In horizontal D.P.C., thickness of cement concrete (1:2:4) is
explain: A standard plinth-level DPC using 1:2:4 concrete is typically 4 cm (approx. 1.5 inches) thick, providing a sufficient barrier against capillary moisture while remaining structurally sound.

q: 3. An ordinary concrete may be made water proof by adding
explain: Products like Pudlo and Impermo are integral waterproofing admixtures, while Snowcem is a waterproof cement paint; all are used to enhance the moisture resistance of concrete structures.

q: 4. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known
explain: Curing is the maintenance of moisture and temperature conditions to allow concrete to develop its intended strength and durability.

q: 5. Slump test in used for
explain: The slump test is a field test used to measure the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 6. Water cement ratio for M10 concretes should be
explain: M10 is a lean concrete mix; a water-cement ratio of 0.65 is typically used to ensure enough hydration for this grade.

q: 7. The mortar in which both cement and lime are used as binding materials, is called
explain: Gauged mortar is a combination of cement and lime, offering the strength of cement with the workability of lime.

q: 8. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) makes up 60-67% of Portland cement, being its primary constituent.

q: 9. The unit weight of RCC is taken as
explain: Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) has a standard density of 2500 kg/m³, which equals 2.5 t/m³.

q: 10. When first class bricks are immersed in water for one hour, the weight of water absorbed by them should not exceed ..........
explain: First-class bricks should not absorb more than 1/6th (approx. 15-20%) of their dry weight in water after 24 hours of immersion.

q: 11. A continuous series of steps between landings is called ..........
explain: A flight is an uninterrupted sequence of steps between two floor levels or landings.

q: 12. To facilitate draining off rain water from the coping, sills, sunshades, a groove is cut on the underside of these and this groove is known as
explain: Throating (or a drip groove) breaks the surface tension of water, forcing it to drop off the edge rather than running back toward the wall face.

q: 13. In a fact roofed building, the roof is made water proof by coating hot bitumen and this coating is done at the rate of
explain: The standard rate for a single coat of hot bitumen for waterproofing a flat roof surface is 1.65 to 1.67 Kg per square meter.

q: 14. The irregular triangular portion of the arcade, formed between the two arches is called as
explain: Spandrils are the triangular spaces found between adjacent arches or between an arch and a rectangular enclosure.

q: 15. The characteristic strength of a material is defined as the strength below which ..........
options: not more than 5 % of the results fall
not less than 5 % of the results fall
not more than 50 % of the results fall
not more than 25 % of the results fall
explain: The characteristic strength is a statistical value ensuring that 95% of test results meet or exceed the specified strength.

q: 16. To facilitate quick flow of a rain water on R.C.C. flat roof towards spouts, it is usually given slope of ..........
explain: Flat roofs are never perfectly flat; a slight gradient of 1 in 40 to 1 in 60 (approx 2-3°) is provided to prevent water ponding.

q: 17. Stone chips or broken bricks are also known as ..........
explain: Spalls are small fragments of stone or brick that break off during cutting or due to weathering/impact.

q: 18. Which of the following is not the standard wattage of electrical lamps?
explain: Standard incandescent bulb wattages traditionally follow increments like 40W, 60W, 75W, and 100W; 50W is not a standard incandescent rating.

q: 19. Grade of concrete generally not used in RCC is
explain: M10 is a lean mix used for levelling or mud mats, not for structural reinforced concrete.

q: 20. Which of the following is not the usual size of the ceiling fans?
explain: Standard sweep sizes for ceiling fans are typically 900mm (36"), 1200mm (48"), and 1400mm (56"); 1000mm is uncommon.

q: 21. Depth of lean concrete bed at the bottom of the footing is ..........
options: equal to its projection beyond wall base
equal to half the width of wall in the super structure
explain: The thickness of the lean concrete (PCC) bed is typically made equal to the horizontal offset (projection) to ensure uniform load distribution.

q: 22. The advantage of air entrained concrete in lining walls and roofs is ............
explain: Air-entrained concrete contains tiny air bubbles which reduce thermal conductivity, making it a better heat insulator.

q: 23. In the case of R.C.C. roof slabs covered by insulating layers, the maximum spacing of expansion joints is ..........
explain: For R.C.C. slabs with insulation, the standard spacing for expansion joints is typically between 20 to 30 meters.

q: 24. In the road works the slump of concrete commonly adopted is ..........
explain: Road construction requires very dry or stiff concrete (low workability) to handle heavy compaction, hence a low slump of 20-28 mm is used.

q: 25. A foundation consisting of thick reinforced concrete slab covering the entire area of the bottom of the structure, is known as ..........
explain: A raft or mat foundation is a continuous slab that supports all the columns and walls of a structure.

q: 26. The pre-stressed concrete piles as compared to pre-cast and reinforced concrete piles ..........
explain: Pre-stressed piles are efficient because the high-strength steel and pre-compression allow for smaller sections with higher durability and load capacity.

q: 27. For the pre-cast reinforced concrete piles, the quality of concrete recommended is ..........
explain: M150 to M200 (approx. M15 to M20) is the minimum grade used to ensure the pile can handle the severe stresses of hammer impact.

q: 28. In the pre-cast reinforced concrete piles, the thickness of concrete covering the main bars should not be less than ..........
explain: A minimum clear cover of 40 mm is required for standard piles to protect the reinforcement from soil-based corrosion.

q: 29. The minimum of covering of the reinforcement for the pre-cast reinforced piles used in sea water, is ..........
explain: Due to the highly corrosive nature of chloride in seawater, the cover is increased to 75 mm to prevent the steel from rusting.

q: 30. The cement which is commonly used in all types of structures and require no special consideration is called ..........
explain: Normal setting cement (OPC) is the general-purpose cement used for most construction tasks.

q: 31. The additional of surfactants in the concrete mix results in ..........
options: decrease in the water cement ratio
increase in the strength of concrete
increase in the density of concrete
explain: Surfactants (admixtures) like plasticizers reduce water requirements, which leads to higher density and strength.

q: 32. The slump commonly adopted for concrete for road works is ..........
explain: Concrete used in road construction needs to be stiff to withstand the vibration of paving machines; a low slump of 25-50 mm is standard.

q: 33. The slump commonly adopted for concrete for columns is ..........
explain: Columns often have dense reinforcement, requiring higher workability (slump of 50-100 mm) to ensure the concrete flows into all spaces without honeycombing.

q: 34. A block of stone or concrete provided under the end of tie beam to spread the load from the roof over a large of bearing, is called ..........
explain: A template (or bed block) is placed under beams or trusses to distribute concentrated loads over a larger area of the supporting masonry.

q: 35. The shell roof may be designed as ...........
options: both thin shell and thick shell
explain: Shell structures can be classified based on their thickness-to-radius ratio; thin shells rely on membrane action, while thick shells consider transverse shear.

q: 36. The roof, suitable for large assembly hall, will be a ...........
explain: Shell roofs are ideal for large assembly halls because they can cover vast spans without the need for internal pillars or columns.

q: 37. In asbestos cement corrugated sheet roofing, the minimum horizontal lap in meters should be ...........
explain: A minimum end (horizontal) lap of 150mm (0.15m) is required to prevent water from entering through the joints during heavy rain.

q: 38. Poisons ratio for concrete
explain: Poisson's ratio for concrete typically ranges between 0.15 to 0.20 and generally increases slightly with richer (stronger) mixes.

q: 39. Minimum grade of concrete to be used in R.C.C. as per I.S. 456: 2000 is
explain: IS 456:2000 specifies that for reinforced concrete work, a grade lower than M20 should not be used (M15 was the limit in the 1978 version).

q: 40. In concrete mix design, allowance for bulking of sand is necessary in case of
explain: Bulking increases the volume of sand but not its weight. Therefore, it only affects volume batching, where adjustments must be made to ensure the correct amount of sand is added.

q: 41. The continuous strain which the concrete undergo due to application external loads is called
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation (strain) of concrete under a constant sustained load.

q: 42. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: While used for setting time, the initial requirement for Vicat's apparatus is to find the 'Normal Consistency' (P) of the cement paste.

q: 43. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds
explain: To ensure reliability, the individual variation in strength between specimens should not exceed ±15% of the average; 1.5 N/mm² is a standard threshold in many texts.

q: 44. In slump test, each layer of concrete is compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and 16 mm diameter for
explain: The slump test procedure requires the concrete to be filled in four layers, with each layer being tampered 25 times.

q: 45. The grade of concrete M150 means that compressive strength of a 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: In the old metric system, M150 denotes a characteristic compressive strength of 150 kg/cm² (equivalent to M15 in N/mm²).
